title: Payment Allocation Standard for Customers Holding Several Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreements
content:
**Standard.** When a customer with more than one Self-Storage Unit Rental Agreement makes a payment without naming the unit it is for, the payment is applied first to the rental whose delinquency date is earliest, then to the next-earliest, and only then to rentals that are current; rentals with no delinquency date are taken in order of move-in date, oldest first. A payment that names a unit is applied only to that unit's agreement and never spills to another agreement; any excess stays on that agreement as a credit balance. Within one agreement the payment is applied in the class's payment application order: the oldest billing period first, and within a billing period its fees before its rent. One payment is split into one payment entry per agreement it reaches, and the entry amounts add up to the payment taken.

The delinquency date of a rental is the due date of the oldest unpaid billing period of its current delinquency cycle; a current rental has none.

## Order of application across agreements

1. Rentals carrying a delinquency date, earliest delinquency date first.
2. Rentals with no delinquency date, earliest move-in date first.

## Order of application within one agreement

1. The oldest billing period with anything unpaid.
2. Within that period, its fees before its rent.
3. Then the next billing period, in the same way.

## Illustration (hypothetical agreements)

A customer holds four units: unit A, delinquent since 3 February; unit B, delinquent since 20 January; unit C, current, moved in during 2019; unit D, current, moved in during 2021. A payment that names no unit is applied to unit B first, then unit A, then unit C, then unit D. The ledger shows one payment entry on each agreement the payment reached, and those entries add up to the amount taken.

If the same customer names unit D, the whole payment is applied to unit D; whatever exceeds unit D's balance due stays on unit D as a credit balance and is not moved to unit A or unit B.

Within unit B, if its January period carries a late fee and unpaid rent and its February period carries unpaid rent, the payment reaches the January late fee, then the January rent, then the February rent.
